high.title: Peso May Test New Lows on Oil Price Surge
high.summary: The Philippine Peso closed at a fresh all-time low of P61.847 per USD on Friday, declining 9.7 centavos from P61.75 the prior session. An intraday trough of P61.85 also marked a new historic weak point. Year-to-date, the Peso has depreciated P3.057 or approximately 4.94%, signaling sustained and accelerating selling pressure. The primary driver is the escalating Iran conflict, which is pushing global oil prices sharply higher and reigniting domestic inflation concerns — a particularly damaging combination for a net oil-importing economy like the Philippines. For FX traders, the psychological P62.00 level is the key threshold to watch; a break above it could trigger further stop-loss selling and accelerate depreciation. The BSP's response — whether it intervenes via spot USD sales or accelerates rate guidance — will be critical. Bond investors should also monitor pass-through inflation risks that could force the BSP to pause or reverse its easing cycle. PHP bears remain in control near-term absent a de-escalation in the Middle East.

high.title: Government Securities Yields Jump on Inflation Fears
high.summary: Philippine government securities (GS) yields surged an average of 19.98 basis points week-on-week as of July 24, based on PHP Bloomberg Valuation Service Reference Rates published on the Philippine Dealing System. The broad-based selloff was driven by dual headwinds: soaring global oil prices tied to the Iran conflict and the Peso's slide to successive all-time lows, both of which intensify domestic inflation expectations. Rising yields reflect investors demanding higher compensation for inflation and currency risk, effectively tightening financial conditions even absent a formal BSP policy move. For bond investors, this is a significant repricing event — a near-20 bps average weekly jump is material and suggests the market is front-running potential BSP policy action or at minimum pricing out further rate cuts. Duration risk is elevated. The upcoming T-bill and T-bond auctions this week will serve as critical price-discovery events. Weak auction demand or high bid-to-cover ratios at elevated rates would confirm that the selloff has further to run. Watch the 5- and 10-year tenors closely as bellwethers for medium-term rate trajectory.

high.title: Debt Rates May End Mixed Amid Iran War and Oil Price Risks
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) is scheduled to auction P50 billion in T-bills this Monday — P20 billion each in 91-day and 182-day papers, and P10 billion in 364-day securities — with no cash management bills offered this week. Additionally, a dual-tenor T-bond auction targeting up to P50 billion is planned for Tuesday. Market analysts anticipate mixed rate outcomes, as the inflationary overhang from surging oil prices amid the Iran conflict creates upward pressure on longer-dated yields, while shorter tenors may remain relatively anchored by BSP liquidity dynamics. For traders, these auctions are the most immediate market-moving events of the week. Mixed results — with short-end rates steady but long-end yields rising — would confirm a steepening bias in the Philippine yield curve, a bearish signal for duration-heavy bond portfolios. Any surprise in the bid-to-cover ratios or awarded rates versus secondary market levels will provide real-time insight into institutional appetite for Philippine government debt under current risk conditions. The dual-tenor T-bond offer is particularly important to watch given elevated GS yield volatility.

high.title: Philippine Exports Worth $6.25 Billion Exposed to 12.5% US Tariff — DTI
high.summary:
A preliminary DTI assessment using 2025 trade data confirms that approximately 34.28% of Philippine exports to the US — valued at $6.25 billion — are directly exposed to the new 12.5% US import tariff. This is a material macro risk for the Philippines' external sector and carries direct FX implications. A sustained deterioration in export receipts would widen the trade deficit, compress the current account, and reduce USD inflows — all of which place structural downward pressure on the Philippine Peso (PHP). For bond traders, a weaker trade balance could stoke inflation concerns (via import pass-through on a softer PHP) and complicate the BSP's easing path, potentially pushing yields higher at the short to medium end of the curve. PSEi-listed exporters and manufacturing conglomerates are also directly in the crosshairs. Investors should monitor whether the Marcos administration pursues a bilateral tariff negotiation with Washington, as any positive outcome could rapidly reverse PHP headwinds. This story warrants close attention as a key macro risk driver in the near term.

---

high.title: Philippine Peso Falls to Fresh Record Low vs US Dollar
high.summary: The Philippine peso broke through a critical technical floor on July 24, closing at 61.847 against the USD — a fresh all-time low — after briefly touching 61.85 intraday. This surpasses the previous record low of 61.75 that had held since late April. The immediate catalyst appears to be rising oil prices, which worsen the Philippines' import bill and current account dynamics, adding structural selling pressure on the peso. Year-to-date, the peso has depreciated approximately 5%, making it one of Asia's worst-performing currencies.

high.title: Key implications for traders and investors:
Peso Rebounds as US, Iran Pause Attacks
high.summary:
The Philippine peso staged a sharp recovery on Monday, strengthening by 17.2 centavos to close at P61.675 per dollar, partially reversing Friday's record-low close of P61.847 — the weakest level on record for the currency. The rebound was driven by easing global crude oil prices over the weekend following a pause in hostilities between the United States and Iran, which reduced the risk premium embedded in energy-linked emerging market currencies. The peso opened the session at P61.76, suggesting intraday buying pressure was sustained throughout the day.

**Why it matters:** The PHP remains highly sensitive to oil price dynamics given the Philippines' status as a net energy importer. A sustained de-escalation in the Gulf would reduce the country's import bill, ease current account pressure, and support the peso. However, the recovery from a record low underscores structural vulnerability. FX traders should monitor whether P61.675 holds as near-term support or whether the record low of P61.847 is retested on any renewed geopolitical flare-up. BSP intervention posture and any follow-through dollar demand from fuel importers will be key variables to watch this week.

high.title: T-Bill Yields Decline on Strong Investor Demand
high.summary:
The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) achieved a full award of its P50 billion T-bill offering on Monday, with total tenders reaching P134.519 billion — nearly three times the amount on offer — as robust investor appetite drove yields lower across all tenors. The strong bid-to-cover ratio signals significant liquidity in the domestic financial system and a renewed appetite for short-duration government paper. The easing of global crude oil prices amid hopes of Middle East de-escalation provided an additional sentiment boost, reducing near-term inflation risk perceptions among domestic bond investors.

**Why it matters:** The near-3x oversubscription and declining yields are a strongly bullish signal for the Philippine government bond market. For bond investors, this suggests the market is pricing in a more benign inflation and monetary policy outlook in the near term. The BTr's ability to raise funds at lower costs reduces fiscal pressure and supports sovereign credit metrics. Watch whether this demand extends to longer-duration bonds in upcoming auctions, which would signal a more durable rally in the Philippine rates market. Any reversal in oil prices or peso weakness could quickly unwind this momentum.

high.title: Philippine Banks' Assets Hit New High of P31 Trillion
high.summary:
Philippine banks' combined assets reached a record P31.128 trillion as of end-June 2026, according to preliminary BSP data. This represents a robust 10.34% year-on-year expansion from P28.211 trillion and a 2.25% month-on-month gain, surpassing the previous all-time high of P30.442 trillion recorded at end-May. The asset base is primarily supported by lending activity, suggesting sustained credit expansion across the banking system. For bond investors, this signals continued strong demand for peso-denominated assets and healthy bank balance sheets that can absorb government paper issuances. For FX traders, a well-capitalized and expanding banking sector reduces systemic risk and supports PHP stability. The BSP's monetary policy stance — including recent rate adjustments — appears to be transmitting effectively into the real economy without triggering asset quality deterioration. Watch for the BSP's next policy meeting for guidance on whether this credit momentum influences future rate decisions, and monitor non-performing loan ratios for signs of stress amid the growth surge.

---

high.title: AMRO Sees Philippines Posting Third Fastest Inflation in ASEAN+3 This Year
high.summary:
The ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO) has revised its 2026 Philippine inflation forecast slightly downward to 5.7% (from 6.0% previously), while holding its 2027 projection at 4.1%. Despite the modest downward revision, the Philippines is still projected to record the third-highest inflation rate among ASEAN+3 economies in 2026 — a sharp acceleration from just 1.7% in 2025. This represents the highest inflation print in recent memory and carries significant implications across asset classes. For FX traders, sustained above-target inflation constrains the BSP's ability to ease monetary policy aggressively, which could provide some floor for the PHP, though elevated prices also risk eroding real purchasing power and widening the current account deficit via import demand. For bond investors, the outlook suggests that Philippine government bond yields may remain under upward pressure as markets price in a prolonged restrictive policy stance. The key variables to monitor include BSP's rate-setting response at upcoming Monetary Board meetings, rice and energy price trajectories, and whether inflation expectations become unanchored — all of which would meaningfully impact PHP/USD direction and the yield curve shape.

---

medium.title: BSP Securities Rate Inches Up Amid Strong Demand
medium.summary:
The average rate on BSP's 28-day short-term securities edged marginally higher for a second consecutive week, even as demand remained robust — total tenders reached P62.179 billion against a P40 billion offering, though this was down from P70.69 billion the prior week. The near-stable rate on BSP bills suggests the central bank is not yet signaling a tightening bias through its open market operations, maintaining a steady liquidity absorption stance. For FX and rates traders, this is a nuanced signal: strong demand for BSP bills indicates banks are still parking excess liquidity at the central bank rather than deploying it, which could limit credit expansion but also reflects caution in the interbank market. The slight rate uptick, even if marginal, warrants monitoring — if BSP bills begin repricing meaningfully higher in coming weeks, it could be an early indicator that the BSP is allowing short-end rates to drift up in response to inflation and Peso weakness, ahead of any formal policy rate adjustment.

---

medium.title: Philippine Banking Industry Hopes Interest Rate Swaps Will Overtake FX Market
medium.summary: The Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP), through Open Market Committee Chair and Citi Philippines CEO Paul Raymond Favila, signaled ambitions for the interest rate swap (IRS) market to surpass FX market volumes — potentially as early as 2026. This reflects a broader push to deepen and diversify Philippine financial markets beyond the traditionally dominant FX segment. For bond and rates traders, a more liquid and active IRS market would enhance hedging capabilities for Philippine government bond positions, improve price discovery for benchmark rates, and reduce transaction costs for duration management. Greater IRS depth would also facilitate foreign investor participation in local currency bond markets, as offshore funds typically require robust derivatives infrastructure before scaling up local bond exposure. Watch for BSP regulatory support and any formal market development initiatives from BAP as catalysts.

medium.title: PHL Banks' NPL Ratio Slips to 6-Month Low
medium.summary: BSP preliminary data shows the Philippine banking sector's gross nonperforming loan (NPL) ratio improved to 3.29% in June — a six-month low — down from 3.44% in May and 3.34% a year prior. The BSP attributed the improvement partly to easing inflation, which has made debt servicing more manageable for borrowers. This is a modestly positive signal for Philippine bank stocks listed on the PSEi, as lower NPL ratios reduce provisioning pressure and support earnings visibility. From a macro perspective, a healthier banking sector reinforces the transmission mechanism of BSP monetary policy and supports the case for continued rate easing. Bond investors should note that improved credit quality generally reduces systemic risk premia, offering a supportive backdrop for Philippine sovereign spreads.

medium.title: Worsening Iran Conflict to Weigh on PHL Shares
medium.summary: The PSEi closed at 6,281.01 on Friday, down 0.03% on the day and down 123.1 points week-on-week from 6,404.11, reflecting mounting investor caution driven by escalating geopolitical tensions around Iran and associated inflation risks. The broader all-shares index also declined 0.13% to 3,422.48. Sentiment is further complicated by President Marcos Jr.'s State of the Nation Address, which markets will parse for fiscal and economic policy signals. Geopolitical risk from the Iran conflict is particularly relevant for PHP and PSEi given the Philippines' high oil import dependency — sustained elevated oil prices would pressure the current account, weigh on the peso, and potentially keep BSP on hold or in a tightening bias, creating a headwind for equities. Investors should monitor SONA policy announcements and any escalation in the Middle East conflict closely.

medium.title: Shares Sink to 6,200 Range as Peso Revisits Low
medium.summary: The PSEi fell 1.04% (65.95 points) to 6,267.85 on Wednesday, marking a second consecutive session of losses as the peso's return to record-low territory rattled investor confidence and triggered profit-taking. The all-shares index shed 0.53% to 3,421.35. The simultaneous deterioration in both the equity market and the currency underscores a **risk-off feedback loop** — peso weakness signals macro stress (inflation, current account pressures), which in turn dampens equity sentiment. For fund managers, this dual pressure on PHP and PSEi highlights the importance of monitoring FX stabilization as a precondition for a sustained equity recovery. The 6,200 level represents near-term technical support to watch.

medium.title: Stocks Inch Higher on Bargain Hunting After Slump
medium.summary: The PSEi recovered modestly on Thursday, gaining 0.24% (15.27 points) to close at 6,283.12, as bargain hunters stepped in after two consecutive days of heavy selling. The broader all-shares index also edged up 0.16% to 3,427.07. However, the rebound was shallow and volumes were likely cautious, suggesting the bounce reflects tactical positioning rather than a fundamental shift in sentiment. Geopolitical concerns remain unresolved, and with the peso still near record lows, any equity recovery will be fragile. This brief stabilization should be viewed in the context of the broader weekly decline of 123 points, reinforcing a **sell-on-rally** bias until FX and geopolitical headwinds materially ease.

medium.title: PSEi Falls on Profit Taking, Growing Gulf Tensions
medium.summary:
The PSEi fell 1.27% (81.92 points) to close at 6,333.80 on Tuesday, July 21, snapping a four-day winning streak as investors engaged in profit-taking following the recent market rally. Sentiment was additionally weighed down by fresh inflation risks stemming from peso weakness and fuel price hikes linked to escalating Gulf tensions. The broader all-shares index also declined 0.32% to 3,439.58. For equity investors, the interplay between geopolitical risk, currency weakness, and imported inflation represents a key headwind for PSEi valuations, particularly for energy-sensitive and consumer-facing sectors. The article predates the subsequent peso rebound (July 28), suggesting market conditions may have partially improved since this print.

---

medium.title: Philippines to Be 4th Slowest-Growing ASEAN Economy This Year — AMRO
medium.summary: AMRO has maintained its Philippine GDP growth forecast at 4.1% for 2026 and 5.5% for 2027, positioning the Philippines as Southeast Asia's fourth slowest-growing economy this year. Key headwinds cited include heavy reliance on imported oil and a weak investment climate, though spillovers from the Middle East conflict are assessed as limited. For FX traders, a below-regional-average growth trajectory could weigh on the PHP over the medium term, as it may dampen foreign investor appetite for Philippine equities and bonds relative to higher-growth ASEAN peers. Bond investors should note that sluggish growth may provide the BSP additional justification for an accommodative bias, potentially capping upside in government bond yields. The investment climate weakness is a key variable to monitor — any improvement via Marcos' reform push (see SONA article) could shift the outlook positively.

medium.title: Marcos Pushes Tax Breaks and Reforms at SONA
medium.summary: President Marcos used his fifth State of the Nation Address to call on Congress to pass a suite of tax measures, including broader income tax exemptions for low- and middle-income earners and tax relief for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The proposals signal the administration's intent to stimulate domestic consumption and formalize the MSME sector in the final stretch of Marcos' term. For bond markets, expanded tax exemptions — if enacted — could pressure fiscal revenues and widen the fiscal deficit, potentially increasing government borrowing requirements and pushing bond yields higher. For PHP and PSEi investors, the reform agenda could be a mild positive for consumer sentiment and corporate earnings in the medium term, but near-term fiscal risk warrants close attention. Legislative progress and the Department of Finance's revenue offset measures will be critical variables to watch.

medium.title: BDO Net Income Hits P40.7 Billion in First Half
medium.summary: BDO Unibank, the Philippines' largest bank by assets, posted H1 2026 net income of P40.7 billion, marginally above the P40.6 billion recorded in the same period last year, with return on equity at 12.7%. Net interest income grew 11% year-on-year, underpinned by a 15% expansion in gross customer loans to P3.9 trillion. As the system's largest lender, BDO's steady performance reinforces the broader narrative of a healthy banking sector, supporting PSEi financials and overall market confidence. For bond investors, BDO's robust loan growth signals strong monetary policy transmission and confirms sustained credit demand, which has implications for the BSP's rate path assessment.

medium.title: UnionBank's First-Semester Net Income Jumps 113%
medium.summary: UnionBank recorded a 113% surge in H1 2026 net income to P6.9 billion, driven by a 9% rise in net revenues to P43.1 billion and improved asset quality. Net interest margin expanded by 40 basis points to 6.9%, reflecting favorable repricing dynamics and growth in higher-yielding consumer loans. The sharp profit recovery is noteworthy for PSEi equity investors tracking financial sector earnings momentum. For rates watchers, the NIM improvement suggests banks are benefiting from the current interest rate environment, which could temper BSP urgency to cut rates aggressively as bank profitability remains strong.

medium.title: Philippines Urged to Resolve Structural Issues to Draw More Foreign Investments
medium.summary: GlobalSource Partners Principal Advisor Diwa C. Guinigundo warned that the Philippines must treat its recent FDI slump as a "wake-up call" and urgently implement structural reforms to restore investor credibility. Weak FDI inflows are a critical concern for the PHP and the balance of payments, as sustained foreign investment shortfalls reduce a key source of long-term USD inflows, placing additional depreciation pressure on the peso. For fund managers, declining FDI momentum also signals deteriorating structural competitiveness relative to ASEAN peers, which could weigh on Philippine equity valuations and risk premium over the medium term. This story warrants continued monitoring, particularly for any government policy response or reform announcements that could serve as a catalyst for renewed capital inflows and PHP stabilization.

medium.title: PSEi Climbs to 6,300 Range as Middle East Tensions Ease
medium.summary: The PSEi gained 0.54% (+33.89 points) to close at 6,314.90 on Monday, supported by bargain hunting and optimism surrounding a de-escalation of Middle East geopolitical tensions, which contributed to a decline in global oil prices. The broader All Shares Index also rose 0.37% to 3,435.37. Lower oil prices, if sustained, are a net positive for the Philippines as a major oil importer — easing imported inflation pressure, supporting the current account, and providing indirect relief for the PHP. Equity traders should watch whether this geopolitical-driven rally has staying power, particularly given the elevated domestic inflation backdrop highlighted by AMRO, which could cap upside if the BSP signals a hawkish hold.
